name: 0.08mm Glass Clear Supported @Solder
notes: 0.08mm Glass Clear @Solder with supports turned on and the proven release geometry from 0.20mm Standard @Solder carried over whole: tree(auto) organic, support_interface_top_layers 0, support_interface_bottom_layers 2, support_base_pattern_spacing 2.5, support_interface_spacing 0.5, support_object_xy_distance 0.35, support_line_width 0.38, support_on_build_plate_only 1, support_critical_regions_only 1, tree_support_branch_distance 6. GAP IS 0.24, WHICH IS THREE 0.08 LAYERS. The layer-aligned rule still applies and the layer here is 0.08, not 0.20, so the numbers from the thicker presets do not transfer: 0.4 would be five layers of unsupported span and would sag badly, 0.2 is not a whole number of layers at all. 0.24 sits between Standard's proven 0.2 mm and Support Easy's 0.4 mm in absolute terms while landing on a layer boundary. TWO THINGS FIGHT EACH OTHER IN THIS FILE AND NEITHER IS A BUG. A support contact face is a matte scar, and on transparent plastic a matte scar is the most visible defect there is - the clear presets set enable_support 0 for that reason. And the paired filament preset Numakers PETG-HS Clear @Solder runs 0% fan at every layer, which is what fuses the interfaces that make the part clear, and is also what makes every bridge over a support sag. Supports on a clear part are therefore a last resort after orientation has failed. Rotate the part first; a face tipped past 30 degrees needs no support at all and leaves no scar to polish out. Put the show face on a smooth PEI plate. Where a scar is unavoidable, plan to sand and coat it - a clear lacquer or epoxy coat fills the ridges and index-matches them, which is the reliable way back to glass. UNTESTED. Nothing has printed on this preset. Run E_CAL_START / E_CAL_RESULT and dry the spool first; both outrank every value in this file.
